text:
StatusBot: INCIDENT ALERT — Service: inference-api, symptom: spike in 503s for POST /v1/generate, count: 2.3k errors/min, paging oncall @Maya Patel. Incident ID: INC-2026-0423-37

Maya Patel: seeing it, joining. allocating pager slot. investigating ingress and autoscaler first.

Maya Patel: quick check — cluster nodes are healthy, but load on runtime-pool-3 is at 96%. logs show repeated RPC timeouts to model-serving instances.

Samir Gupta: I can take runtime-side. grabbing logs from runtime-pool-3 and checking gRPC queue backlog.

Liam O'Neil: I noticed a recent canary deploy to optimized-kernel v2.1 ~ 30m ago. Could be a regression. DeployBot, can you confirm rollout percentage?

DeployBot: Canary deploy optimized-kernel:v2.1 -> traffic 25% across region-us-east-1. No automatic rollback triggered.

Samir Gupta: confirmed increased tail latency in nodes with optimized-kernel:v2.1. p50 fine but p99 >> 10s. looks like a kernel path regression under long sequences.

Maya Patel: mitigation plan: 1) throttle traffic to v2.1 canary (shift back to v2.0) 2) enable fallback routing for requests > 1024 tokens to keep latency SLOs 3) page CS for customer impact assessment.

Liam O'Neil: command to shift traffic:
```bash
redwoodctl rollout set-traffic optimized-kernel:v2.0 --percentage 100 --selector region=us-east-1
```
I'm running it now.

DeployBot: traffic shift initiated. expected completion ~ 30s.

StatusBot: NOTE — traffic reallocation in progress. Error rate decreasing but still elevated.

Maya Patel: Samir — can you restart the model-serving processes on affected nodes to clear stuck KV caches while rollback finishes? Keep rolling restarts with 30s delay.

Samir Gupta: doing rolling restarts, 5 nodes at a time. ETA 8 minutes.

Liam O'Neil: v2.1 traffic at 0% in us-east-1 now. monitoring.

StatusBot: Error rate down to 0.4k errors/min from 2.3k. Latency p99 trending back under 2.5s.

Maya Patel: good. declare mitigation in place. starting timeline capture for post-incident notes. Need statuspage update and a CS customer notification draft for impacted customers (notably AcmeApps and BrightApps). @Anya Rodriguez can you own customer comms?

Anya Rodriguez: on it. draft below for statuspage+CS DM — please review/edit: 
"We experienced elevated 503 errors affecting inference requests between 22:43 and 23:06 UTC due to an internal runtime regression introduced in a canary kernel rollout. Traffic was shifted back to the previous kernel and nodes were restarted; service is stable. No customer data was accessed or exposed. If you saw failures, retrying requests should succeed. For customers requiring a detailed timeline or SLA credit assessment, please reach out to cs@redwood.ai."

Maya Patel: nit: include incident ID and mitigation start/end times. Also call out that long-sequence requests were affected more.

Anya Rodriguez: updated: 
"Incident INC-2026-0423-37: Between 22:43 and 23:06 UTC customers may have seen 503 errors for generation requests, primarily affecting long-sequence jobs (>1024 tokens). Cause: regression in optimized-kernel:v2.1 canary. Mitigation: canary traffic reverted to v2.0 at 22:48 UTC and rolling restarts completed by 23:04 UTC. Service stable as of 23:06 UTC. If you experienced customer-impacting failures, please contact your CS rep or cs@redwood.ai for timeline and SLA support."

Samir Gupta: suggest adding internal note: root cause suspected as incorrect integer overflow check in KV cache hotpath under corner sequence length; reproducer in internal test harness.

Liam O'Neil: adding short technical blurb for statuspage / internal incident timeline (for engineering readers).

Maya Patel: fine. I'll post a StatusPage component update once we confirm stable for 10m. Anyone object?

CrisisCommander: thumbs up from incident commander. Also capture action items for postmortem and CS followup.

StatusBot: Statuspage update queued. Message preview:
"We've restored generation API performance after mitigating an internal runtime regression. Affected requests: long-sequence generation in us-east-1. Customer impact window: 22:43–23:06 UTC. Root cause under investigation. For updates see: link-to-incident-doc."

Maya Patel: posting now.

StatusBot: Statuspage updated at 23:12 UTC.

Anya Rodriguez: CS DMs queued to impacted accounts with tailored timeline and offer for post-incident call. Draft DM snippet for AcmeApps: 

"Hi AcmeApps team — we saw 503s on generation requests impacting long-sequence workloads between 22:43 and 23:06 UTC. We reverted a canary kernel and restarted affected nodes; service is stable. We're preparing a short RCA and are happy to schedule a call. If you'd like a credit assessment for SLA impact, let us know and we'll expedite."

Maya Patel: good. also ask CS to capture customers who had retries that resulted in duplicated charges or inconsistent outputs — we need to know candidate cases for compensation.

Anya Rodriguez: will track. tagging affected-customer list and creating follow-up ticket in CS queue.

Samir Gupta: quick technical note for timeline:
- 22:40 UTC: kernel v2.1 canary reached 25%
- 22:43 UTC: increased 503s observed, paging fired
- 22:45 UTC: oncall triage — suspected tail latency regression in canary
- 22:48 UTC: traffic shifted back to v2.0 (mitigation start)
- 22:55 UTC: rolling restarts underway
- 23:04 UTC: restarts complete
- 23:06 UTC: error rate returned to baseline
- 23:12 UTC: statuspage updated

Maya Patel: thanks. I'll own the postmortem doc and include reproducer and the fix: revert faulty check and add a unit/regression test for high-token KV cache flows; also include a canary traffic rollback automation improvement.

Liam O'Neil: action items I’ll own: 1) add regression test to CI, 2) add a canary monitoring alert for p99 > threshold on canary nodes, 3) automate immediate rollback when p99 > 5s for >5% of traffic.

CrisisCommander: recovery ok. For CS follow-up: request that Anya provides an RCA summary and proposed preventative actions by EOD tomorrow, plus a prioritized list of customers for proactive outreach. Also prepare a templated message for SLA credit offers.

Anya Rodriguez: will deliver RCA summary + customer outreach list by EOD tomorrow. Initial ask: does engineering have a tentative estimate of whether this counts as an SLA-qualifying outage?

Maya Patel: rough estimate — affected error volume and duration suggest it may trigger SLA calculations for customers with strict uptime clauses. I'll provide exact metrics in the postmortem (token-normalized error counts per customer).

StatusBot: Incident INC-2026-0423-37 — mitigation complete, incident status: resolved (monitoring). Closing notes: follow-up postmortem scheduled, CS outreach in progress.

Anya Rodriguez: thanks team. I'll cross-post the CS drafts in #customer-success and link to the incident doc for context.

Maya Patel: handing off to postmortem owner. Samir, Liam — please add your logs, prometheus graphs, and reproducer steps into the incident doc.

Samir Gupta: added logs and reproducer.

Liam O'Neil: added deployment diffs and alert thresholds.

Maya Patel: signing off from pager. leaving incident owner to CrisisCommander for post-incident coordination.

CrisisCommander: acknowledged. Incident thread archived to incident doc; next steps: postmortem draft in 48h, CS RCA + outreach list EOD tomorrow, prioritized engineering fixes in next sprint. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
